wiki_catalogs.name: Project Overview
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Create comprehensive content for this section focused on the Kardenwort project. Explain its purpose as an intelligent command-line utility for language learners that processes text to generate Anki flashcards. Describe the core philosophy of separating reading from study, medium independence, offline-first approach, and simplifying complex linguistic analysis. Document the key features including intelligent lemmatization with spaCy, advanced German compound word splitting, user-trainable lemma override system, rich context provision, dual card types (word and sentence), hierarchical deck creation from Markdown headers, and integration with Anki and GoldenDict-ng. Explain the relationship between the core engine, Anki CSV importer, and Anki templates in the Kardenwort ecosystem. Include practical examples of how language learners and educators use the tool with authentic texts. Address common issues like German genitive correction and noun capitalization. Highlight performance considerations for processing large texts and best practices for achieving optimal results.

wiki_catalogs.name: Text Processing Pipeline
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Create comprehensive content for this section focused on the text processing pipeline of Kardenwort. Explain the two main modes: word extraction (vocabulary cards) and sentence processing (contextual cards), detailing their distinct mechanisms and use cases. Describe the hybrid sentence splitting mechanism that automatically chooses between line-by-line processing and spaCy's grammatical sentence tokenization based on input format. Document the pipeline stages: initialization with spaCy models and dictionaries, text ingestion from various sources, tokenization and lemmatization with German compound splitting, collection and sorting of unique lemmas, TSV and JSON metadata generation, and Anki import orchestration. Explain the role of the `kardenwort_runner.py` script in automating this workflow. Include practical examples demonstrating the processing of both single-line and multi-line inputs. Address common issues related to text encoding (UTF-8 requirement) and line-by-line correspondence in parallel texts. Highlight performance considerations for processing large documents and best practices for optimal accuracy.

wiki_catalogs.name: Lemma Override System
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for the lemma override system, a core advanced feature of Kardenwort. Explain how users can correct and customize lemmatization results using the `lemma_override_de.tsv` and `lemma_override_en.tsv` files. Document the three-tiered priority system (priority1, priority2, priority3) and their matching logic: exact lemma+word, exact word, and exact lemma. Describe the support for context-aware rules using plain text and regex conditions (e.g., 'regex:(?<!^)Ihr') to apply overrides only in specific sentence contexts. Provide concrete examples from the provided TSV files, such as correcting 'Daten' to 'Daten' only when preceded by 'bibliografische', or fixing possessive pronouns like 'Ihr' not at the start of a sentence. Explain the file format: tab-separated values with columns for Spacy Lemma, Original Word, Target Lemma, and Context. Detail how the `load_lemma_override_rules` function parses these files, handles malformed lines, and builds an in-memory rule structure. Include implementation specifics from `get_overridden_lemma_for_word` and `find_matching_override_in_context`, including regex compilation, error handling, and rule precedence. Address common issues such as regex syntax errors, rule conflicts, and cases where overrides are not applied due to incorrect context or capitalization. Provide troubleshooting guidance and best practices for creating effective override rules to improve flashcard accuracy.

wiki_catalogs.name: Windows CMD Scripts
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Create comprehensive content for this section focused on the pre-configured Windows CMD scripts in the `scripts/run/cmd/` directory. Explain their purpose as convenient entry points for Windows users to execute Kardenwort with specific processing configurations without manually typing complex command-line arguments. Document the naming convention of the scripts, breaking down components such as language (de/en), input mode (w=with file, ws=with stdin, lp=lemma per line), processing type (t=token, s=sentence), mode (s=single, m=medium, l=large, t1/t2/t3), output target (anki/console), and versioning (v1/v2/v3). Detail the specific processing scenarios each script covers, such as generating word cards with Anki import, sentence cards with console output, or mixed modes. Highlight the dependency on `_config_loader.cmd` for reading configuration from `config.ini`. Include practical examples of invoking these scripts from the command line. Address the critical limitation of single-line processing when used with stdin and provide guidance on when to use these scripts versus direct Python invocation. Explain how these scripts streamline common workflows for users who prefer double-click execution or integration with file associations.

wiki_catalogs.name: Hierarchical Deck Creation
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for the hierarchical deck creation feature. Explain how Kardenwort parses Markdown headers (e.g., #, ##) in source text to automatically generate nested Anki deck structures. Describe the role of the `parse_markdown_for_branch_headers` function in identifying branch points in the header hierarchy and the `process_parallel_text_files` function in managing the deck stack (`deck_stack` and `level_stack`) as it processes each line. Detail how header levels determine deck nesting, with higher-level headers (e.g., #) creating parent decks and lower-level headers (e.g., ##, ###) creating subdecks. Explain the naming convention that uses a numeric prefix (e.g., 100001-) combined with a sanitized version of the header text to ensure unique and ordered deck names. Cover the integration with the `--anki-markdown-decks` and `--anki-create-subdecks` command-line arguments, and how the `--anki-parent-deck` option sets a root deck. Describe the automatic generation of deck description metadata via `_write_deck_metadata`, which can include the source text, translations, or per-deck content based on the `--anki-deck-content` flag. Provide practical examples of Markdown input and the resulting Anki deck hierarchy. Address edge cases such as consecutive headers of the same level, missing headers, and non-header content. Include troubleshooting guidance for decks not being created as expected, such as incorrect header syntax or misconfigured command-line arguments.

wiki_overview.content:
<blog>
# Comprehensive Project Analysis: Kardenwort

## 1. Project Introduction

### Purpose Statement
Kardenwort is a specialized text processing tool designed to extract linguistic elements (words and sentences) from source texts and prepare them for import into Anki, a popular spaced repetition flashcard application. The system focuses on German and English languages, with particular emphasis on German compound word handling and morphological analysis.

### Core Goals and Objectives
The primary objectives of Kardenwort are:
- Extract lemmatized tokens and sentences from source texts
- Process parallel texts with context preservation
- Generate Anki-compatible TSV files with rich linguistic metadata
- Support hierarchical deck creation based on document structure
- Handle German compound word splitting and morphological variations

### Target Audience
The tool is designed for language learners, educators, and researchers who use Anki for vocabulary acquisition, particularly those studying German and English. It's especially valuable for users who want to create custom flashcards from authentic texts while preserving linguistic context and relationships.

## 2. Technical Architecture

### Component Breakdown
The Kardenwort system consists of several interconnected components that work together to process text and generate flashcards:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[User Input] --> B[Shell Scripts]
    B --> C[kardenwort_runner.py]
    C --> D[config.ini]
    C --> E[kardenwort.py]
    E --> F[spaCy NLP Models]
    E --> G[Lemma Override Rules]
    E --> H[German Compound Splitter]
    C --> I[Anki CSV Importer]
    I --> J[Anki Application]
    
    style A fill:#f9f,stroke:#333
    style J fill:#f9f,stroke:#333
```

### Design Patterns
The project employs several design patterns:
- **Wrapper Pattern**: `kardenwort_runner.py` acts as a wrapper around the core processing logic
- **Configuration-Driven Design**: Extensive use of `config.ini` for runtime configuration
- **Pipeline Processing**: Text flows through a series of processing stages
- **Modular Architecture**: Clear separation between core functionality and execution scripts

### System Relationships
The system components interact in a coordinated pipeline:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Input[Input Text Files] --> Runner[kardenwort_runner.py]
    Config[config.ini] --> Runner
    Runner --> Core[kardenwort.py]
    Core --> NLP[spaCy NLP Processing]
    Core --> GCS[German Compound Splitter]
    Core --> Output[TSV Output]
    Output --> Importer[Anki CSV Importer]
    Importer --> Anki[Anki Application]
    
    classDef component fill:#e1f5fe,stroke:#1565c0;
    class Runner,Core,Importer component;
```

### Data Flow Diagram
The data flows through the system in a structured pipeline:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Source[Source Text] --> Preprocessing[Text Preprocessing]
    Preprocessing --> Tokenization[Tokenization with spaCy]
    Tokenization --> Lemmatization[Lemmatization]
    Lemmatization --> Compound[German Compound Splitting]
    Compound --> Override[Lemma Override Rules]
    Override --> Deduplication[Deduplication]
    Deduplication --> Context[Context Extraction]
    Context --> Formatting[TSV Formatting]
    Formatting --> Output[Output File]
    Output --> Import[Anki Import]
    
    style Source fill:#ffecb3,stroke:#ffa000
    style Output fill:#c8e6c9,stroke:#388e3c
    style Import fill:#f8bbd0,stroke:#c2185b
```

## 3. Key Implementation

### Main Entry Points
- **kardenwort_runner.py** (src/kardenwort/core/kardenwort_runner.py): Primary entry point that orchestrates the entire process
- **kardenwort.py** (src/kardenwort/core/kardenwort.py): Core processing logic
- **Shell scripts** (a/sh/*.sh): Convenience scripts for common operations

### Core Modules
- **kardenwort.py** (src/kardenwort/core/kardenwort.py): Implements lemmatization, compound splitting, and TSV generation
- **kardenwort_runner.py** (src/kardenwort/core/kardenwort_runner.py): Manages configuration, execution flow, and Anki integration

### Configuration Approach
- **config.ini** (config.ini): Central configuration file with environment settings, paths, and default parameters
- **config.ini.template** (config.ini.template): Template for configuration setup
- Environment variables and command-line arguments provide additional configuration options

### External Dependencies
- **pyproject.toml** (pyproject.toml): Project metadata and Python package dependencies
- **spaCy** (de_core_news_lg, en_core_web_lg): Natural language processing models
- **german_compound_splitter**: Specialized library for German compound word splitting

### Integration Points
- **Anki CSV Importer**: Integration with external Anki import tool
- **GoldenDict**: Configuration file suggests integration with dictionary application
- **External scripts**: Various Python scripts in the 'a' directory for specialized processing

### Component Relationship Diagram
```mermaid
graph TD
    Runner[kardenwort_runner.py] --> Config[config.ini]
    Runner --> Core[kardenwort.py]
    Runner --> Importer[Anki CSV Importer]
    Core --> spaCy[spaCy NLP]
    Core --> GCS[german_compound_splitter]
    Core --> Data[data/]
    Core --> Output[results/]
    Config --> Runner
    Config --> Core
    Data --> Core
    Output --> Importer
    
    classDef module fill:#4fc3f7,stroke:#0288d1;
    classDef config fill:#81c784,stroke:#388e3c;
    classDef external fill:#ffb74d,stroke:#f57c00;
    class Runner,Core module
    class Config config
    class Importer,spaCy,GCS external
```

## 4. Key Features

### Functionality Overview
Kardenwort provides comprehensive text processing capabilities focused on language learning:

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Idle
    Idle --> Configuration: Load config.ini
    Configuration --> Processing: Start processing
    Processing --> TextAnalysis: Analyze input text
    TextAnalysis --> Lemmatization: Extract lemmas
    Lemmatization --> CompoundSplitting: Process German compounds
    CompoundSplitting --> ContextExtraction: Extract sentence context
    ContextExtraction --> OutputGeneration: Generate TSV
    OutputGeneration --> AnkiImport: Import to Anki
    AnkiImport --> Complete: Success
    Processing --> Error: Processing error
    Error --> Complete: Failure
    Complete --> Idle: Reset
```

### Implementation Highlights
- **Multilingual Support**: Handles both German and English with language-specific processing
- **Compound Word Handling**: Advanced German compound word splitting with configurable options
- **Context Preservation**: Maintains sentence context for better language learning
- **Flexible Output**: Generates TSV files compatible with Anki's import system
- **Hierarchical Decks**: Supports creating nested deck structures based on document headings

### Feature Architecture
```mermaid
graph TD
    A[Input Processing] --> B[Language Detection]
    B --> C{German?}
    C -->|Yes| D[Compound Splitting]
    C -->|No| E[Standard Processing]
    D --> F[Lemma Override Rules]
    E --> F
    F --> G[Deduplication]
    G --> H[Context Extraction]
    H --> I[TSV Generation]
    I --> J[Anki Import]
    
    style A fill:#bbdefb,stroke:#1976d2
    style J fill:#c8e6c9,stroke:#388e3c
    style D fill:#ffccbc,stroke:#d84315
```

Sources:
- [kardenwort.py](src/kardenwort/core/kardenwort.py)
- [kardenwort_runner.py](src/kardenwort/core/kardenwort_runner.py)
- [config.ini](config.ini)
- [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml)
</blog>
